name: Post-Communist Legacy
description: Decades of central planning left weak markets but a broad welfare habit. Institutions are still maturing.

name: Strong Institutions
description: Courts, civil service, and central bank command real independence and public trust.

name: Weak Institutions
description: Rules bend to whoever holds power this month; the state struggles to deliver.

name: Trade-Oriented Economy
description: An open, export-driven economy — prosperous when the world buys, exposed when it doesn't.

name: Agricultural Economy
description: A large rural sector: stable and self-reliant, but slower to grow and modernise.

name: High Corruption
description: Patronage and graft siphon off public capacity and quietly erode trust.

name: Low Corruption
description: Clean government: public money mostly reaches its purpose.

name: Federal State
description: Power is shared with strong regions — resilient, but harder to steer from the centre.

name: Centralized Government
description: Authority concentrates in the capital — decisive, but brittle if the centre falters.

name: Resource Wealth
description: Oil, gas, or minerals fill the treasury — a cushion of easy money that also warps the economy around whoever controls the spigot.

name: Militarist State
description: The armed forces are a pillar of the regime — disciplined and assertive abroad, expensive and coup-prone at home.

name: Ethnic Fault Lines
description: Deep communal divisions run under every institution; grievances travel fast and the centre is never fully trusted by the periphery.

name: Theocratic Authority
description: Political legitimacy flows from religious authority — a unifying source of order for believers, an exclusionary one for everyone else.

name: Young Democracy
description: Democratic institutions are real but recent — enthusiastic, untested, and easily strained by their first serious crisis.
